questions.stem: How does a data fabric differ from a data hub?
options: The fabric is a storage system; the hub is a governance tool
The hub is the distribution and operationalisation layer, while the fabric is a broader paradigm unifying governance, integration and orchestration across the whole enterprise
The fabric replaces the hub entirely
They are the same concept under different vendor names
The hub works in the cloud; the fabric works on-premises only
questions.explanation: Both break down silos but operate at different levels of abstraction: the hub distributes insights back to applications, while the fabric unifies governance, integration and orchestration across all data assets.

questions.stem: Which stages of the data lifecycle does a data fabric coordinate?
options: Only storage and backup
Discovery, integration, governance, security and consumption
Only ETL scheduling
Only reporting and dashboards
Only encryption and decryption
questions.explanation: The data fabric coordinates the entire lifecycle of data: discovery, integration, governance, security and consumption.

questions.stem: Which metaphor is used to describe the data fabric within the enterprise?
options: The skeleton of the enterprise
The central nervous system of the enterprise
The bloodstream of the enterprise
The immune system of the enterprise
The lungs of the enterprise
questions.explanation: The fabric is likened to the central nervous system: each data platform performs its own function, but the fabric, like the brain, ensures they work together under consistent policies.

questions.stem: Why is the data fabric particularly relevant today?
options: Because all data now lives in one central database
Because most organisations operate in a hybrid and multi-cloud reality with data spread across on-premises systems, private clouds and multiple public clouds
Because relational databases have been abandoned
Because regulators require a single vendor
Because data volumes have shrunk
questions.explanation: Data is distributed across on-premises, private cloud and multiple public clouds; without a unifying architecture this creates integration gaps, inconsistent governance and compliance risks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the capabilities a data fabric provides?
options: Centralised governance and policy enforcement across platforms
Metadata-driven intelligence to automate discovery, lineage and integration
Security and compliance controls applied consistently in all environments
Physical consolidation of all data into a single warehouse
Self-service access for business and technical users
questions.explanation: The fabric provides governance, metadata-driven intelligence, consistent security, hybrid and multi-cloud integration and self-service access; it does not physically consolidate all data into one warehouse.

questions.stem: Is the data fabric a single tool or product?
options: Yes, it is a specific software product
Yes, it is a cloud service offered by one vendor
No, it is a set of technologies and practices spanning catalogues, metadata platforms, orchestration engines, API gateways and governance frameworks
No, it is purely a policy document
Yes, it is a database engine
questions.explanation: The data fabric is not a single tool or product but a set of technologies and practices that together create a logical fabric woven across the enterprise.

questions.stem: What role does metadata-driven intelligence play in a data fabric?
options: It encrypts data at rest
It automates data discovery, lineage and integration
It replaces the data warehouse
It stores transactions in real time
It generates dashboards for executives
questions.explanation: Metadata-driven intelligence in the fabric automates data discovery, lineage and integration.

questions.stem: Across which kinds of data assets does a data fabric provide its unified layer of governance and control?
options: Only data lakes
Only OLTP systems
OLTP systems, data warehouses, data lakes, lakehouses and BI platforms alike
Only cloud-hosted systems
Only BI platforms
questions.explanation: The fabric provides governance and control across all data assets, whether they reside in OLTP systems, data warehouses, data lakes, lakehouses or BI platforms.

questions.stem: What does self-service access mean in the context of a data fabric?
options: Users can install their own databases
Business and technical users can discover and consume governed data themselves
Users can bypass access controls
Applications manage their own pipelines
Data is available without any metadata
questions.explanation: Self-service access lets business and technical users discover and consume governed data without waiting on bespoke integration.

questions.stem: Which phrase describes the data fabric's position in modern data ecosystems?
options: The brain coordinating activity across a distributed digital enterprise
The vault storing all historical facts
The pipeline moving data into the warehouse
The dashboard presenting KPIs
The archive for retired data
questions.explanation: The architectural shift positions the data fabric as the brain of modern data ecosystems, coordinating activity across an increasingly distributed digital enterprise.
